title: Conditional Quantum Flow Matching for Data-Scarce Physiological Signal Augmentation
abstract: Generative augmentation is a standard remedy for label scarcity in physiological signal classification, but existing quantum generative models start from uninformative noise, ignoring class structure that is already available. We propose Conditional Quantum Flow Matching (CQFM): a single 306-parameter circuit, conditioned on both flow time and class label, transports a compact class-conditional prior toward the target distribution. Quantum flow matching as published is unconditional, so this is to our knowledge the first conditional one, and the first EEG augmentation on a parameterized quantum circuit. A nonnegative spectral embedding removes the need for tomography at readout. On BCI Competition IV-2a, starting from a prior rather than noise is worth $+5.1$ accuracy points over QuDDPM (9/9 subjects), though at that operating point a class-conditional Gaussian matches CQFM. Where the prior fails the transport earns its keep: given one transferred from other subjects it regains $+7.2$ TSTR points (9/9).
summary: This paper introduces Conditional Quantum Flow Matching (CQFM), a novel quantum generative model designed to augment data-scarce physiological signals like EEG by incorporating class structure. CQFM conditions its quantum flow on both time and class label, allowing it to utilize an informative prior rather than starting from pure noise. The model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in signal augmentation tasks.
main_problem: Generative augmentation is needed for label scarcity in physiological signal classification, but existing quantum generative models ignore available class structure by starting from uninformative noise.
main_result: The proposed Conditional Quantum Flow Matching (CQFM) significantly outperforms baselines, achieving a +5.1 accuracy point gain over QuDDPM on BCI Competition IV-2a.
method: CQFM is a novel quantum generative model that conditions the flow matching process on both the flow time and the class label, enabling the transport of an informative class-conditional prior.
model_or_system: The model is applied to physiological signals, specifically EEG, using a 306-parameter parameterized quantum circuit. The input data is first processed via a spectral embedding to create a nonnegative feature vector.
key_observables: Augmented downstream MLP accuracy, C2ST (real-vs-generated discriminability), LSD (class-mean log-spectral distance), and TSTR (Test statistic for class structure reproduction).
important_parameters: The model is conditioned on flow time ($t$) and class label ($c$); the circuit has 306 parameters.
main_assumptions: The encoding is limited to feature-space augmentation, and the quantum advantage is questioned as the model is classically simulable.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the encoding process, the flow step comparison between CQFM and QuDDPM, and performance comparisons showing CQFM's superiority when using informative priors.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the CQFM mechanism using conditional parameterization, presents ablation studies showing the necessity of the informative prior, and validates performance on the BCI dataset.
why_interesting: It applies quantum machine learning techniques (quantum circuits for generative modeling) to complex, structured data like physiological signals, bridging quantum computation with advanced ML for signal processing.
